name: Aphids
hosts: Vegetables, fruits, cereals, legumes, ornamental plants
symptoms: Stunted growth and leaf curling Yellowing or mottling of leaves Honeydew deposits on leaves and stems Sooty mold growth reducing photosynthesis Transmission of plant viruses
description: Small sap-sucking insects affecting many crops and ornamental plants. Rapid reproduction via telescoping generations allows populations to multiply quickly. Some species alternate between host plants; others are generalists. They produce honeydew, which leads to sooty mold growth. Aphids act as vectors for plant viruses.
management: Release of predatory insects and parasitoids Encourage natural enemies in gardens or greenhouses Use of fungal biopesticides (Beauveria, Lecanicillium, Metarhizium)
prevention: Monitor populations using yellow-pan or Moericke traps Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization to reduce aphid attraction Remove infested plant parts promptly Encourage mutualistic ants only in controlled environments Crop rotation and maintaining plant health
